"""
The PCA axes tool: reduce many measured variables to PC1 and PC2 per grain.

Writes the scores back into the spreadsheet as columns, so every other tool
picks them up as ordinary dimensions — a PDP of PC1, a top-down unmix along
PC1, a bivariate density over PC1 x PC2.

The fit is global, over every grain of every selected sample at once. That is
what keeps a mixture of populations a convex combination after the transform,
and so what makes unmixing along a derived axis valid.
"""
from antioch.elements import Div, P

from plot_lib import bar_trace
from sed_stats import pca

from .dataset import categories_of, is_numeric_column
from .plots import make_plot
from .tables import result_table

CAPTION_STYLE = {"font-size": "13px", "color": "#555", "margin": "0 0 6px 0"}
NOTE_STYLE = {"color": "#6c757d"}

# Column names written back to the sheet. Rerunning overwrites them.
AXIS_COLUMNS = ("PC1", "PC2")


class AxesProblem(ValueError):
    """The PCA cannot be fitted with what was chosen; the message says why."""


def run_axes(charts, rows, sample_col, dimensions, opts, in_workflow=False):
    """
    Fit the grain PCA.

    Returns:
        (updated_rows, report): a copy of `rows` with PC1 and PC2 filled in
        (grains missing a variable get blanks), and the element describing the
        fit. The input rows are not changed.

    Raises:
        AxesProblem: with fewer than two variables, or no usable grains
    """
    variables = [d for d in dimensions if d not in AXIS_COLUMNS]
    if len(variables) < 2:
        raise AxesProblem("Choose at least two variables to reduce.")

    selected = opts.get("samples")
    columns = _encode_variables(rows, sample_col, variables, selected)
    complete, matrix = _complete_rows(rows, sample_col, columns, selected)
    if len(matrix) < 2:
        raise AxesProblem("No grains have a value for every chosen variable.")
    names = [name for column in columns for name in column.names]
    column_weights = [w for column in columns for w in column.weights]

    weights = None
    if opts.get("grain_weighting") == "sample":
        weights = _sample_weights([row for row, _ in complete], sample_col)

    result = pca.grain_pca(matrix, variables=names, n_components=2,
                           weights=weights, column_weights=column_weights)
    updated = _write_scores(rows, complete, result)

    scored = len(complete)
    total_rows = len([r for r in rows
                      if selected is None
                      or str(r.get(sample_col, "") or "").strip() in selected])
    where = ("PC1 and PC2 are now columns in this step's table — the steps "
             "after it will offer them as dimensions."
             if in_workflow else
             "PC1 and PC2 are now columns in the spreadsheet — every other tool "
             "will offer them as dimensions. To see the grains, use Scatterplot "
             "with x = PC1 and PC2 as the y dimension; choose \"One plot per "
             "sample\" to compare samples side by side.")
    wrapper = Div(
        P(f"{scored} of {total_rows} grains scored on "
          f"{len(variables)} standardized variables"
          f"{_encoding_note(columns)}. "
          f"PC1 explains {result.percent(0):.1f}% and PC2 "
          f"{result.percent(1):.1f}% of the variance between grains.",
          style=CAPTION_STYLE),
        P(where, style=CAPTION_STYLE),
        _loadings_table(result),
    )
    if scored < total_rows:
        wrapper.add(P(f"{total_rows - scored} grains were left blank for "
                      f"missing a value.", style=NOTE_STYLE))
    if opts.get("scree"):
        wrapper.add(*_scree_section(charts, result))
    return updated, wrapper


class _Column:
    """
    One chosen variable as it enters the fit.

    A numeric variable is one column. A categorical one is a block of 0/1
    indicator columns, one per category, each down-weighted by 1/sqrt(k) so the
    block as a whole counts as a single variable.
    """

    def __init__(self, variable, categories=None):
        self.variable = variable
        self.categories = categories
        if categories is None:
            self.names = [variable]
            self.weights = [1.0]
        else:
            self.names = [f"{variable} = {c}" for c in categories]
            self.weights = [len(categories) ** -0.5] * len(categories)

    def encode(self, raw):
        """This variable's matrix entries for one grain, or None if unusable."""
        if raw in ("", None):
            return None
        if self.categories is None:
            try:
                return [float(raw)]
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                return None
        value = str(raw).strip()
        if value not in self.categories:
            return None
        return [1.0 if value == c else 0.0 for c in self.categories]


def _encode_variables(rows, sample_col, variables, selected):
    """Numeric variables as themselves; anything else one-hot over its categories."""
    columns = []
    for variable in variables:
        if is_numeric_column(rows, variable):
            columns.append(_Column(variable))
        else:
            columns.append(_Column(variable, categories_of(
                rows, sample_col, variable, selected)))
    return columns


def _encoding_note(columns):
    categorical = [c for c in columns if c.categories is not None]
    if not categorical:
        return ""
    count = sum(len(c.categories) for c in categorical)
    return (f", {len(categorical)} of them categorical and one-hot encoded into "
            f"{count} columns")


def _complete_rows(rows, sample_col, columns, selected):
    """
    Rows usable for the fit, paired with their index in the original table.

    A grain missing any one variable has no position in the variable space, so
    it is scored as blank rather than imputed.
    """
    complete = []
    matrix = []
    for index, row in enumerate(rows):
        sample = str(row.get(sample_col, "") or "").strip()
        if selected is not None and sample not in selected:
            continue
        values = []
        for column in columns:
            encoded = column.encode(row.get(column.variable, ""))
            if encoded is None:
                values = None
                break
            values.extend(encoded)
        if values is None:
            continue
        complete.append((row, index))
        matrix.append(values)
    return complete, matrix


def _sample_weights(rows, sample_col):
    """1/n per grain, so every sample pulls on the axis equally."""
    counts = {}
    for row in rows:
        sample = str(row.get(sample_col, "") or "").strip()
        counts[sample] = counts.get(sample, 0) + 1
    return [1.0 / counts[str(row.get(sample_col, "") or "").strip()]
            for row in rows]


def _write_scores(rows, complete, result):
    """Copy the rows with PC1/PC2 filled in; unscored grains get blanks."""
    updated = [dict(row) for row in rows]
    for row in updated:
        for column in AXIS_COLUMNS:
            row[column] = ""

    for position, (_, index) in enumerate(complete):
        for axis, column in enumerate(AXIS_COLUMNS):
            if axis < result.scores.shape[1]:
                updated[index][column] = f"{float(result.scores[position, axis]):.6g}"
    return updated


def _loadings_table(result):
    """What the axes mean, in terms of the variables that made them."""
    body = []
    # Ordered by influence on PC1, so the axis reads top-down.
    for variable, loading in result.loadings(0):
        column = result.variables.index(variable)
        second = (float(result.components[1, column])
                  if result.components.shape[0] > 1 else 0.0)
        body.append([variable, f"{float(loading):+.3f}", f"{second:+.3f}"])

    return Div(
        P("Loadings — a variable with a large positive weight pushes grains "
          "toward the positive end of that axis; opposite signs mean the axis "
          "is a trade-off between those variables.",
          style={**CAPTION_STYLE, "margin": "16px 0 6px 0"}),
        result_table(
            ["Variable",
             f"PC1 ({result.percent(0):.1f}%)",
             f"PC2 ({result.percent(1):.1f}%)"],
            body,
        ),
    )


def _scree_section(charts, result):
    ratios = [float(r) * 100 for r in result.explained_ratio_all]
    names = [f"PC{i + 1}" for i in range(len(ratios))]
    trace = bar_trace(names, ratios, "Explained variance", color="#3b6fb6")

    caption = P("Scree plot — how much of the grain-to-grain variance each "
                "component carries. A steep drop after PC1 means one axis "
                "captures most of it; a shallow one means reducing to two "
                "axes throws real information away.",
                style={**CAPTION_STYLE, "margin": "16px 0 6px 0"})
    plot = Div(make_plot(
        charts, [trace], "PCA axes — scree", "Component", "% variance",
        height=320, show_legend=False, filename="pca_axes_scree",
        extra_layout={"xaxis": {"title": {"text": "Component"}, "type": "category"}},
    ).element)
    return caption, plot

"""Chart construction shared by the builders.

`charts` is always the running list of (name, PlotlyChart) pairs for the output
being built; the output window uses it for resizing and for the SVG/zip export, so
every plot has to be registered there as it is made.
"""
from plot_lib import PlotlyChart

from .config import CHART_WIDTH


def make_plot(charts, traces, title, x_title, y_title, height=420,
              show_legend=True, filename=None, extra_layout=None):
    """Build a plot and register it under `filename` for export."""
    name = filename or title.replace(" ", "_")
    layout = {
        "title": {"text": title},
        "xaxis": {"title": {"text": x_title}},
        "yaxis": {"title": {"text": y_title}, "rangemode": "tozero"},
        "showlegend": show_legend,
        "legend": {"orientation": "v", "x": 1.02, "y": 1},
        "barmode": "group",
    }
    if extra_layout:
        layout.update(extra_layout)

    chart = PlotlyChart(
        traces=traces,
        layout=layout,
        config={"toImageButtonOptions": {"format": "svg", "filename": name}},
        width=CHART_WIDTH,
        height=height,
    )
    charts.append((name, chart))
    return chart
scripts/dashboard/ports.py:
"""
Choosing what a node's input port reads.

A port reads one source, or — for a graph that can draw several series — as
many as the user adds with "+ Add input". The same editor sits in the dialog
that adds a step and on the step's row afterwards, so wiring is changed the
way it was made.
"""
from antioch.elements import Button, Div, Option, Select, Span
from antioch.event import when

ROW_STYLE = {"display": "flex", "align-items": "center", "gap": "6px",
             "margin-bottom": "4px"}
ADD_STYLE = {
    "background-color": "#eef1f4", "color": "#333", "border": "1px solid #cfd6dd",
    "padding": "2px 9px", "cursor": "pointer", "font-size": "12px",
    "border-radius": "3px",
}
MUTED = {"color": "#6c757d", "font-size": "12px"}


class PortEditor:
    """
    A list of source pickers for one port.

    Args:
        port: the `workflow_lib.Port` being wired
        choices: `[(source id, label), ...]` the port could read
        chosen: the source ids it reads now
        on_change: called with the new list of ids whenever it changes
        empty_text: what to say when there is nothing to connect

    A port that takes one source shows one picker. A `multiple` port shows
    one per source, each removable, with "+ Add input" below; an `optional`
    one may have none.
    """

    def __init__(self, port, choices, chosen=None, on_change=None,
                 empty_text="Nothing to connect yet."):
        self.port = port
        self._choices = list(choices)
        self._chosen = list(chosen) if chosen is not None else self._default()
        self._on_change = on_change
        self._empty_text = empty_text
        self.element = Div()
        self._build()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ state

    def sources(self):
        """The ids this port reads, in the order they were added."""
        return list(self._chosen)

    def set_choices(self, choices):
        """Offer different sources, keeping the ones that are still on offer."""
        self._choices = list(choices)
        offered = {value for value, _ in self._choices}
        kept = [value for value in self._chosen if value in offered]
        self._chosen = kept or (self._default() if not self.port.optional else [])
        self._build()

    def _default(self):
        """
        A single source to start from: the latest step that fits, so a new step
        reads what was just made — except a table, where the spreadsheet is the
        safer start.
        """
        if not self._choices or self.port.optional:
            return []
        wants_table = "table" in self.port.types
        return [self._choices[0 if wants_table else -1][0]]

    def _notify(self):
        if self._on_change:
            self._on_change(self.sources())

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- display

    def _build(self):
        box = self.element
        box._dom_element.innerHTML = ""
        if not self._choices:
            box.add(Span(self._empty_text, style=dict(MUTED)))
            return
        for index, value in enumerate(self._chosen):
            box.add(self._row(index, value))
        if self.port.multiple:
            if self._unused() or not self._chosen:
                add = Button("+ Add input", style=dict(ADD_STYLE))

                @when(add.events.click)
                def on_add(sender, *args):
                    self._add()
                box.add(add)
            else:
                # Nothing left to add; say so rather than leave the user
                # looking for a button that is not there.
                box.add(Span("That is every step that fits. Add more steps to "
                             "draw them together.", style=dict(MUTED)))

    def _row(self, index, value):
        select = Select()
        for source_id, label in self._choices:
            select.add(Option(label, value=source_id))
        select.value = value
        select.on('change', lambda e, i=index, s=select: self._pick(i, s.value))
        row = Div(select, style=dict(ROW_STYLE))
        if self.port.multiple and (len(self._chosen) > 1 or self.port.optional):
            remove = Button("×", style=dict(ADD_STYLE))

            @when(remove.events.click)
            def on_remove(sender, *args):
                self._remove(index)
            row.add(remove)
        return row

    def _unused(self):
        return [value for value, _ in self._choices if value not in self._chosen]

    def _pick(self, index, value):
        self._chosen[index] = value
        self._notify()

    def _add(self):
        spare = self._unused()
        self._chosen.append(spare[-1] if spare else self._choices[-1][0])
        self._build()
        self._notify()

    def _remove(self, index):
        del self._chosen[index]
        self._build()
        self._notify()

"""
Projects (.sedprj) on Google Drive, from a button in the title bar.

A project is the spreadsheet plus the workflow (see `project_lib`); a step's output is made
again by running the workflow. The **Projects** button sits beside the account email and
only appears while Drive is usable; it opens one dialog that holds everything: the projects
Sed/Stats saved (click one to open it), Save, Save as…, and Browse Drive… for a file saved
elsewhere.

Under the `drive.file` scope the app cannot search a whole Drive, so the list
is of the app's own files; a file picked through Browse Drive… is also one the
app may overwrite afterwards.
"""
import asyncio

import js

from antioch.elements import Button, Div, Input, Label, P, Span
from antioch.event import when
from antioch.macros import Modal
from antioch.macros.base import Macro

DEFAULT_NAME = "sed-stats-project"
AUTOSAVE_KEY = "sedStats.autosave"
ERROR_COLOR = "#b00020"
MUTED_COLOR = "#555"

# Everything the app can see that looks like a project: our own type, or the
# extension in the name (a file uploaded by hand has neither our type nor a
# reliable one, so the name has to be allowed to match).
PROJECT_QUERY = (f"(mimeType = '{MIME_TYPE}' or name contains 'sedprj') "
                 f"and trashed = false")

MODAL_STYLE = {"max-width": "540px", "width": "92vw"}
CURRENT_STYLE = {"font-size": "14px", "font-weight": "600", "margin": "0 0 4px 0"}
STATUS_STYLE = {"font-size": "13px", "color": MUTED_COLOR, "margin": "0 0 10px 0",

LIST_STYLE = {"max-height": "40vh", "overflow-y": "auto", "margin": "6px 0 14px"}
ITEM_STYLE = {

    "margin-bottom": "6px", "background-color": "#f6f8fa",
    "border": "1px solid #d8dee4", "border-radius": "4px",

}
ITEM_DATE_STYLE = {"color": "#6c757d", "font-size": "12px", "white-space": "nowrap"}
ACTIONS_STYLE = {"display": "flex", "flex-wrap": "wrap", "gap": "8px"}


class ProjectPanel(Macro):
    """
    The Projects button and the dialog behind it.

    Usage:
        project = ProjectPanel(drive, get_rows=table.get_data,
                               get_workflow=workflow_panel.to_dict)
        header.add(project.button_element)      # beside the account control

        @when(project.events.project_loaded)
        def on_loaded(sender, project, filename): ...

    Fires `load_start(filename)` before reading a file, `project_loaded(project,
    filename)` once it parsed, `saved(rows, workflow)` after anything was written to
    Drive (with exactly what was written), and `error(message)` on any failure.

    The work tracker drives `set_dirty`, `autosave` and the `guard`: the button
    shows a dot while there are unsaved changes, and `guard()` is asked before
    a project replaces the current work.
    """

    def __init__(self, drive, get_rows=None, get_workflow=None, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(macro_type="project_panel", **kwargs)
        self._drive = drive
        self._get_rows = get_rows
        self._get_workflow = get_workflow
        self._save_dialog = None     # built lazily: each mounts itself in the page
        self._menu = None
        self.file_id = None          # the Drive file this project is saved as
        self.name = ""               # its name, without the extension
        self._dirty = False          # unsaved changes, as told by the tracker
        self._busy = False           # a save is in flight; autosave stands aside
        # Awaited before opening a project over the current work; resolves to
        # False to cancel. The app replaces this with the tracker's confirmation.
        async def allow():
            return True
        self.guard = allow

        self._create_event('load_start')
        self._create_event('project_loaded')
        self._create_event('saved')
        self._create_event('error')

        self._init_macro()

    @property
    def configured(self):
        return self._drive.configured

    # -------------------------------------------------------------- elements

    def _create_elements(self):
        # The macro's own container stays empty and unmounted; the only thing
        # placed in the page is the title-bar button.
        container = self._register_element('container', self._create_container({}))
        button = self._register_element(
            'button', Button("Projects", style=dict(ACCOUNT_BUTTON_STYLE)))
        # Hidden until Drive is usable: no project can be opened or saved
        # without it, so there is nothing for the button to offer.
        button.style.display = "none"

        def hover(active):
            button.style.background_color = (
                ACCOUNT_BUTTON_HOVER if active else "transparent")

        button.on_mouseenter(lambda e: hover(True))
        button.on_mouseleave(lambda e: hover(False))

        @when(button.events.click)
        def on_click(sender, *args):
            self._show_menu()

        return container

    @property
    def button_element(self):
        """The title-bar button; place it beside the account control."""
        return self._get_element('button')

    def set_dirty(self, dirty):
        """Mark the button (and the dialog's heading) for unsaved changes."""
        self._dirty = bool(dirty)
        self.button_element.set_text("Projects •" if dirty else "Projects")
        if self._menu is not None:
            self._current.set_text(self._current_text())

    def _current_text(self):
        text = ("Current project: " + project_filename(self.name) if self.file_id
                else "Current project: not saved to Drive yet")
        return text + (" — unsaved changes" if self._dirty else "")

    @property
    def autosave_enabled(self):
        try:
            return js.window.localStorage.getItem(AUTOSAVE_KEY) == "1"
        except Exception:
            return False

    def _remember_autosave(self, enabled):
        try:
            if enabled:
                js.window.localStorage.setItem(AUTOSAVE_KEY, "1")
            else:
                js.window.localStorage.removeItem(AUTOSAVE_KEY)
        except Exception:
            pass  # a preference; blocked site data just means it is not kept

    @property
    def can_autosave(self):
        """Autosave only overwrites a project that already has a Drive file."""
        session = self._drive.session
        return bool(self.file_id and session.signed_in and session.has_drive_access)

    def set_enabled(self, usable):
        """Follow the Drive panel: shown only while signed in with access."""
        if not self.configured:
            return
        self.button_element.style.display = "inline-block" if usable else "none"

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ the dialog

    def _ensure_menu(self):
        if self._menu is not None:
            return
        self._current = P("", style=dict(CURRENT_STYLE))
        self._status = P("", style=dict(STATUS_STYLE))
        self._list = Div(style=dict(LIST_STYLE))

        save = ButtonSuccess("Save", size="small")
        save_as = ButtonSecondary("Save as…", size="small")
        browse = ButtonSecondary("Browse Drive…", size="small")
        close = ButtonSecondary("Close", size="small")

        self._autosave_box = Input("checkbox")
        self._autosave_box._dom_element.checked = self.autosave_enabled
        autosave = Label(
            self._autosave_box,
            Span(" Autosave to Drive — overwrites the open project a few seconds "
                 "after a change. Needs a project already saved to Drive.",
                 style={"font-size": "13px", "color": MUTED_COLOR}),
            style={"display": "block", "margin": "0 0 12px 0", "cursor": "pointer"})

        self._autosave_box.on(
            'change',
            lambda e: self._remember_autosave(self._autosave_box._dom_element.checked))

        @when(save.events.click)
        def on_save(sender, *args):
            asyncio.ensure_future(self._save(save_as=False))

        @when(save_as.events.click)
        def on_save_as(sender, *args):
            asyncio.ensure_future(self._save(save_as=True))

        @when(browse.events.click)
        def on_browse(sender, *args):
            asyncio.ensure_future(self._browse())

        @when(close.events.click)
        def on_close_click(sender, *args):
            self._menu.close()

        body = Div(
            self._current, self._status, self._list, autosave,
            Div(save, save_as, browse, close,
                style=dict(ACTIONS_STYLE)),
        )
        self._menu = Modal(title="Projects", modal_style=MODAL_STYLE)
        self._menu.set_content(body)
        DOM.add(self._menu.element)

    def _show_menu(self, status=None, is_error=False):
        """Open the dialog, refreshed; `status` carries on a message across it."""
        self._ensure_menu()
        self._current.set_text(self._current_text())
        self._autosave_box._dom_element.checked = self.autosave_enabled
        self._set_status("" if status is None else status, is_error)
        self._menu.open()
        asyncio.ensure_future(self._populate())

    def _set_status(self, message, is_error=False):
        if self._menu is None:
            return
        self._status.set_text(message)
        self._status.style.color = ERROR_COLOR if is_error else MUTED_COLOR

    async def _populate(self):
        """Fill the list with the projects Sed/Stats saved, newest first."""
        self._list.clear()
        try:
            found = await self._drive.client.list_files(PROJECT_QUERY)
        except Exception as error:
            self._set_status(f"Could not search Drive: {error}", True)
            return
        projects = [f for f in found
                    if str(f.get("name", "")).lower().endswith(EXTENSION)]
        if not projects:
            self._list.add(P(
                "No projects saved by Sed/Stats yet. Save this one, or use "
                "Browse Drive… to pick a project file from anywhere.",
                style={"font-size": "13px", "color": MUTED_COLOR, "margin": "0"}))
            return
        for project in projects:
            self._list.add(self._item(project))

    def _item(self, project):
        item = Button(style=dict(ITEM_STYLE))
        item.add(Span(project["name"], style={"overflow": "hidden",
                                              "text-overflow": "ellipsis"}),
                 Span(_when(project.get("modifiedTime")), style=ITEM_DATE_STYLE))

        @when(item.events.click)
        def on_click(sender, *args):
            asyncio.ensure_future(self._open_file(project["id"], project["name"]))
        return item

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ open

    async def _browse(self):
        try:
            self._drive._require_drive()
            # No type filter: Drive types an uploaded .sedprj as whatever it
            # guesses, usually octet-stream, so any filter would hide it.
            picked = await self._drive.session.pick_file(None)
        except Exception as error:
            self._set_status(str(error), True)
            return
        if picked:
            await self._open_file(picked["id"], picked["name"])

    async def _open_file(self, file_id, name):
        if not await self.guard():
            return
        # Closed so the loading curtain (and Google's picker) are not behind it.
        self._menu.close()
        try:
            self._drive._require_drive()
            self._fire_event('load_start', name)
            text = await self._drive.client.download_text(file_id)
            project = load_project(text)
        except Exception as error:
            # A ProjectError's message already says what is wrong with the
            # file (not a project, from a newer version, ...).
            self._fire_event('error', str(error))
            self._show_menu(f"Could not open {name}: {error}", is_error=True)
            return

        self.file_id = file_id
        self.name = _stem(name)
        # The workflow comes back with its steps unrun: some (MDS, unmixing) take seconds, so
        # the user runs it when they want its outputs.
        self._fire_event('project_loaded', project, name)

    def adopt_recovered(self, file_id, name):
        """Take the Drive file a recovered session was working on."""
        self.file_id = file_id or None
        self.name = name or ""

    def detach(self):
        """
        Forget the Drive file this project came from.

        Called when other data replaces the spreadsheet, so the next "Save"
        asks where to save instead of overwriting a project with data that is
        not its own.
        """
        self.file_id = None
        self.name = ""

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ save

    def _workflow(self):
        return self._get_workflow() if self._get_workflow else None

    async def _overwrite(self, rows, workflow):
        """Write the current state over the project's Drive file."""
        name = project_filename(self.name)
        await self._drive.client.update(
            self.file_id, dump_project(self.name, rows, workflow=workflow), MIME_TYPE)
        self._fire_event('saved', rows, workflow)
        return name

    async def autosave(self):
        """
        Overwrite the open project quietly; the tracker calls this after a change.

        Never creates a file and never asks anything, so it does nothing unless
        there is already a project to overwrite. A failure is shown in the
        dialog and leaves the work marked unsaved.
        """
        rows = list(self._get_rows() if self._get_rows else [])
        if self._busy or not self.can_autosave or not rows:
            return False
        workflow = self._workflow()
        self._busy = True
        try:
            name = await self._overwrite(rows, workflow)
            self._set_status(f"Autosaved {name}.")
            return True
        except Exception as error:
            self._set_status(f"Autosave failed: {error}", True)
            return False
        finally:
            self._busy = False

    async def _save(self, save_as):
        rows = list(self._get_rows() if self._get_rows else [])
        if not rows:
            self._set_status("Nothing to save — the spreadsheet is empty.", True)
            return
        try:
            self._drive._require_drive()
        except Exception as error:
            self._set_status(str(error), True)
            return
        if self._busy:
            return

        client = self._drive.client
        workflow = self._workflow()
        overwrite = bool(self.file_id) and not save_as

        if overwrite:
            self._busy = True
            self._set_status(f"Saving {project_filename(self.name)}…")
            try:
                name = await self._overwrite(rows, workflow)
            except Exception as error:
                self._set_status(f"Could not save: {error}", True)
                return
            finally:
                self._busy = False
            self._set_status(f"Saved {name} ({_steps(workflow)}).")
            return

        # Asking for a name and folder opens another dialog; this one steps
        # aside so the two are never stacked, and comes back with the result.
        self._menu.close()
        status, is_error = "", False
        self._busy = True
        try:
            if self._save_dialog is None:
                self._save_dialog = SaveDialog(
                    self._drive.session, title="Save project to Google Drive")
            choice = await self._save_dialog.ask(
                project_filename(self.name or DEFAULT_NAME))
            if choice is None:
                return
            name = project_filename(choice["name"])
            result = await client.upload(
                name, dump_project(_stem(name), rows, workflow=workflow),
                mime_type=MIME_TYPE, folder_id=choice["folder_id"])
            self.file_id = result.get("id")
            self.name = _stem(result.get("name", name))
            self._fire_event('saved', rows, workflow)
            status = (f"Saved {result.get('name', name)} to "
                      f"{choice['folder_name']} ({_steps(workflow)}).")
        except Exception as error:
            status, is_error = f"Could not save: {error}", True
            self._fire_event('error', str(error))
        finally:
            self._busy = False
            self._show_menu(status, is_error)


def _steps(workflow):
    """'3 steps' for a status line."""
    count = len((workflow or {}).get("steps") or [])
    return f"{count} step{'s' if count != 1 else ''}"


def _stem(filename):
    """A file name without the project extension."""
    filename = str(filename)
    return filename[:-len(EXTENSION)] if filename.lower().endswith(EXTENSION) else filename


def _when(timestamp):
    """Drive's RFC 3339 time as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC', or blank."""
    text = str(timestamp or "")
    return f"{text[:10]} {text[11:16]} UTC" if len(text) >= 16 else ""

"""
An in-page dialog that asks for one line of text, in place of the browser's `window.prompt`.

For the same reasons as the confirm dialog: the native one can be suppressed (and then answers
"cancel" at once), blocks the page, and cannot validate or say what it is for.
"""
import asyncio

from antioch.dom import DOM
from antioch.elements import Div, Input, Label, P
from antioch.event import when
from antioch.macros import Modal
from component_lib.button import ButtonSecondary, ButtonSuccess

MODAL_STYLE = {"max-width": "420px", "width": "92vw"}
LABEL_STYLE = {"font-size": "13px", "color": "#333", "display": "block", "margin": "0 0 6px 0"}
INPUT_STYLE = {"width": "100%", "box-sizing": "border-box", "padding": "7px 9px", "font-size": "14px",
               "border": "1px solid #cfd6dd", "border-radius": "4px"}
ACTIONS_STYLE = {"display": "flex", "justify-content": "flex-end", "gap": "8px", "margin-top": "14px"}


class PromptDialog:
    """
    Usage:
        dialog = PromptDialog()
        name = await dialog.ask("Rename column", "Column name", "age_Ma")
        # the text, or None if it was cancelled or closed
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self._future = None
        self._label = Label("", style=dict(LABEL_STYLE))
        self._input = Input("text", style=dict(INPUT_STYLE))
        self._ok = ButtonSuccess("OK", size="small")
        self._cancel = ButtonSecondary("Cancel", size="small")

        @when(self._ok.events.click)
        def on_ok(sender, *args):
            self._answer(str(self._input._dom_element.value))

        @when(self._cancel.events.click)
        def on_cancel(sender, *args):
            self._answer(None)

        # Enter accepts, as in any single-line form.
        self._input.on("keydown", lambda e: self._answer(str(self._input._dom_element.value))
                       if e.key == "Enter" else None)

        self.modal = Modal(title="", modal_style=dict(MODAL_STYLE))
        self.modal.set_content(Div(self._label, self._input,
                                   Div(self._cancel, self._ok, style=dict(ACTIONS_STYLE))))
        DOM.add(self.modal.element)

        @when(self.modal.events.close)
        def on_close(sender, *args):
            self._answer(None)

    async def ask(self, title, label, value=""):
        if self._future is not None:
            return None                 # one question at a time
        self.modal.set_title(title)
        self._label.set_text(label)
        self._input._dom_element.value = value or ""
        self._future = asyncio.get_event_loop().create_future()
        self.modal.open()
        # The field is not focusable until the modal is shown.
        asyncio.get_event_loop().call_later(0.05, self._focus)
        return await self._future

    def _focus(self):
        try:
            self._input._dom_element.focus()
            self._input._dom_element.select()
        except Exception:
            pass

    def _answer(self, value):
        future, self._future = self._future, None
        if future is None or future.done():
            return
        self.modal.close()
        future.set_result(value)

"""
The Sample PCA tool: one point per sample, from the samples' distributions.

Where the grain-level tool (pca_axes) fits a PCA across every grain and writes
scores back onto the grains, this one treats each sample as a single
observation. Its features are the sample's distribution for each chosen
dimension — the PDP of an age, the share of each polymer — laid end to end, so
a categorical dimension needs no encoding. Samples that plot close together
have similar distributions, and the loadings say which bins or categories
separate them.
"""
from collections import Counter

import numpy as np

from antioch.elements import Div, P

from plot_lib import bar_trace, categorical_color, line_trace, marker_trace, series_color
from sed_stats import pca
from workflow_lib import NodeProblem

from .dataset import is_numeric_column, series_for, values_by_sample
from .plots import make_plot
from .tables import result_table

CAPTION_STYLE = {"font-size": "13px", "color": "#555", "margin": "0 0 6px 0"}
NOTE_STYLE = {"color": "#6c757d"}
SECTION_STYLE = {**CAPTION_STYLE, "margin": "16px 0 6px 0"}

NO_COLOR = "(none)"
COMPONENT_COLORS = ("#2a78d6", "#eb6834")


def fit_sample_pca(rows, sample_col, dimensions, opts):
    """
    Fit the sample-level PCA.

    Returns:
        (result, samples, labels, categorical, dropped): the fit; the samples
        it covers, in order; each dimension's grid labels; which dimensions are
        categorical; and the samples left out for missing data

    Raises:
        NodeProblem: with no dimensions, or fewer than three samples
    """
    if not dimensions:
        raise NodeProblem("Choose at least one dimension.")

    blocks, labels, categorical, dropped = _feature_blocks(
        rows, sample_col, dimensions, opts)
    samples = blocks["samples"]
    if len(samples) < 3:
        raise NodeProblem("Need at least three samples with data for every "
                          "chosen dimension.")

    matrices = []
    for dimension in dimensions:
        matrix = blocks[dimension]
        if opts.get("clr") and categorical[dimension]:
            matrix = pca.clr(matrix)
        matrices.append((dimension, matrix))
    result = pca.combined_pca(matrices, samples, n_components=2)
    return result, samples, labels, categorical, dropped


def draw_report(charts, result, dimensions, labels, categorical, scree):
    """What drives the map: each dimension's share of each component, the
    loadings across its bins or categories, and optionally the scree plot."""
    wrapper = Div()
    if len(dimensions) > 1:
        wrapper.add(_contribution_table(result))
    for dimension in dimensions:
        wrapper.add(*_loadings_section(charts, result, dimension, labels[dimension],
                                       categorical[dimension]))
    if scree:
        wrapper.add(*_scree_section(charts, result))
    return wrapper


def _feature_blocks(rows, sample_col, dimensions, opts):
    """
    Each dimension as an (n_samples, n_bins) matrix over the samples that have
    data for every dimension.

    Returns:
        (blocks, labels, categorical, dropped) where blocks maps each
        dimension to its matrix and "samples" to the shared row order
    """
    series_by_dimension = {}
    labels = {}
    categorical = {}
    for dimension in dimensions:
        grid, series = series_for(rows, sample_col, dimension, "pdf", opts)
        series_by_dimension[dimension] = dict(series)
        labels[dimension] = list(grid)
        categorical[dimension] = not is_numeric_column(rows, dimension)

    requested = list(opts.get("samples") or [])
    first = series_by_dimension[dimensions[0]]
    order = requested or list(first)
    samples = [s for s in order
               if all(s in series_by_dimension[d] for d in dimensions)]
    dropped = [s for s in order if s not in samples]

    blocks = {"samples": samples}
    for dimension in dimensions:
        blocks[dimension] = np.asarray(
            [series_by_dimension[dimension][s] for s in samples], dtype=float)
    return blocks, labels, categorical, dropped


def color_groups(rows, sample_col, samples, attribute):
    """
    How the sample points are coloured.

    Returns a dict with "legend" (whether a legend helps), and either
    "values" (a number per sample, drawn on a continuous scale), "groups" (an
    ordered {name: [sample indexes]}), or neither for one colour per sample.
    """
    if not attribute or attribute == NO_COLOR:
        return {"legend": False, "title": None}

    grouped = values_by_sample(rows, sample_col, attribute, set(samples))
    if is_numeric_column(rows, attribute):
        means = [(float(np.mean([float(v) for v in grouped[s]])) if s in grouped
                  else float("nan")) for s in samples]
        return {"legend": False, "title": attribute, "values": means}

    labels = [Counter(str(v) for v in grouped[s]).most_common(1)[0][0]
              if s in grouped else "no data" for s in samples]
    groups = {}
    for index, label in enumerate(labels):
        groups.setdefault(label, []).append(index)
    return {"legend": True, "title": attribute, "groups": groups}


def map_traces(xs, ys, samples, colors):
    """The sample points, coloured as `color_groups` says."""
    if "values" in colors:
        return [{
            "type": "scatter", "mode": "markers+text",
            "x": xs, "y": ys, "text": list(samples),
            "textposition": "top center", "textfont": {"size": 10},
            "showlegend": False, "name": "Samples",
            "marker": {"size": 13, "color": colors["values"],
                       "colorscale": "Viridis", "showscale": True,
                       "colorbar": {"title": {"text": colors["title"],
                                              "side": "right"}}},
        }]

    if "groups" in colors:
        return [marker_trace([xs[i] for i in members], [ys[i] for i in members],
                             name, color=categorical_color(k), size=12,
                             labels=[samples[i] for i in members])
                for k, (name, members) in enumerate(colors["groups"].items())]

    return [marker_trace([x], [y], sample, size=12, labels=[sample],
                         color=series_color(i, len(samples)))
            for i, (sample, x, y) in enumerate(zip(samples, xs, ys))]


def _contribution_table(result):
    """How much each dimension drives each component, as percentages."""
    first = dict(result.block_contributions(0))
    second = dict(result.block_contributions(1)) if result.components.shape[0] > 1 else {}
    body = [[name, f"{first[name] * 100:.1f}%",
             f"{second.get(name, 0.0) * 100:.1f}%"] for name in first]
    return Div(
        P("Which dimension drives each component — shares sum to 100% down a "
          "column.", style=SECTION_STYLE),
        result_table(["Dimension", f"PC1 ({result.percent(0):.1f}%)",
                      f"PC2 ({result.percent(1):.1f}%)"], body),
    )


def _loadings_section(charts, result, dimension, labels, is_categorical):
    """PC1 and PC2 loadings across one dimension's bins or categories."""
    start, stop = next((a, b) for name, a, b in result.blocks if name == dimension)
    traces = []
    for axis in range(min(2, result.components.shape[0])):
        values = [float(v) for v in result.components[axis, start:stop]]
        name = f"PC{axis + 1}"
        color = COMPONENT_COLORS[axis]
        traces.append(bar_trace(labels, values, name, color) if is_categorical
                      else line_trace(labels, values, name, color))

    caption = P(f"Loadings across {dimension} — where a component is positive, "
                f"samples rich in that part sit toward the positive end; "
                f"opposite signs are a trade-off.", style=SECTION_STYLE)
    layout = {"yaxis": {"title": {"text": "Loading"}, "rangemode": "normal"}}
    if is_categorical:
        layout["xaxis"] = {"title": {"text": dimension}, "type": "category",
                           "tickangle": -45}
        layout["margin"] = {"l": 60, "r": 20, "t": 50, "b": 110}
    plot = Div(make_plot(
        charts, traces, f"{dimension} — loadings", dimension, "Loading",
        height=340, show_legend=True, filename=f"{dimension}_sample_pca_loadings",
        extra_layout=layout,
    ).element)
    return caption, plot


def _scree_section(charts, result):
    ratios = [float(r) * 100 for r in result.explained_ratio_all]
    names = [f"PC{i + 1}" for i in range(len(ratios))]
    caption = P("Scree plot — variance carried by each component. A steep drop "
                "after PC1 or PC2 means two axes describe the samples well; with "
                "n samples there are at most n − 1 components.",
                style=SECTION_STYLE)
    plot = Div(make_plot(
        charts, [bar_trace(names, ratios, "Explained variance", color="#3b6fb6")],
        "Sample PCA — scree", "Component", "% variance",
        height=320, show_legend=False, filename="sample_pca_scree",
        extra_layout={"xaxis": {"title": {"text": "Component"}, "type": "category"}},
    ).element)
    return caption, plot
scripts/dashboard/save_dialog.py:
"""
The "Save to Drive" dialog: pick a name and a destination folder.

Replaces a bare `js.prompt`, which could only ask for a name and gave the user
no say in where the file landed — everything went to the root of My Drive.

Choosing the folder through Google's own picker is also what makes writing
into it legal under the `drive.file` scope: the app may write where the user
pointed it, and nowhere else.
"""
import asyncio

from antioch.dom import DOM
from antioch.elements import Div, Input, Label, P, Span
from antioch.event import when
from antioch.macros import Modal

from component_lib.button import ButtonSecondary, ButtonSuccess

MODAL_STYLE = {"max-width": "460px", "width": "92vw"}
ROW_STYLE = {"margin-bottom": "14px"}
LABEL_STYLE = {
    "display": "block", "font-size": "13px", "font-weight": "600",
    "margin-bottom": "5px", "color": "#333",
}
INPUT_STYLE = {
    "width": "100%", "box-sizing": "border-box", "padding": "8px 10px",
    "font-size": "14px", "border": "1px solid #ccc", "border-radius": "4px",
}
FOLDER_ROW_STYLE = {
    "display": "flex", "align-items": "center", "gap": "10px",
    "flex-wrap": "wrap",
}
FOLDER_NAME_STYLE = {
    "font-size": "13px", "color": "#333", "flex": "1", "min-width": "0",
    "overflow": "hidden", "text-overflow": "ellipsis", "white-space": "nowrap",
}
ERROR_STYLE = {"font-size": "13px", "color": "#b00020", "margin": "0 0 10px 0"}
ACTIONS_STYLE = {
    "display": "flex", "justify-content": "flex-end", "gap": "8px",
    "margin-top": "18px",
}

MY_DRIVE = "My Drive"


class SaveDialog:
    """
    Asks for a filename and destination, then hands both back.

    Usage:
        dialog = SaveDialog(session)
        choice = await dialog.ask("plot.svg")
        if choice:                      # None when cancelled
            name, folder_id = choice["name"], choice["folder_id"]
    """

    def __init__(self, session, title="Save to Google Drive"):
        self.session = session
        self._future = None
        self._folder_id = None

        self._name = Input("text", style=INPUT_STYLE)
        self._folder_label = Span(MY_DRIVE, style=FOLDER_NAME_STYLE)
        self._error = P("", style=ERROR_STYLE)
        self._error.style.display = "none"

        choose = ButtonSecondary("Choose folder…", size="small")
        reset = ButtonSecondary("My Drive", size="small")
        cancel = ButtonSecondary("Cancel", size="small")
        save = ButtonSuccess("Save", size="small")

        @when(choose.events.click)
        def on_choose(sender, *args):
            asyncio.ensure_future(self._choose_folder())

        @when(reset.events.click)
        def on_reset(sender, *args):
            self._set_folder(None, MY_DRIVE)

        @when(cancel.events.click)
        def on_cancel(sender, *args):
            self.modal.close()

        @when(save.events.click)
        def on_save(sender, *args):
            self._submit()

        # Enter in the name field is the obvious way to accept this dialog.
        self._name.on("keydown", self._on_key)

        body = Div(
            Div(Label("File name", style=LABEL_STYLE), self._name,
                style=ROW_STYLE),
            Div(Label("Destination", style=LABEL_STYLE),
                Div(self._folder_label, choose, reset, style=FOLDER_ROW_STYLE),
                style=ROW_STYLE),
            self._error,
            Div(cancel, save, style=ACTIONS_STYLE),
        )

        self.modal = Modal(title=title, modal_style=MODAL_STYLE)
        self.modal.set_content(body)
        DOM.add(self.modal.element)

        @when(self.modal.events.close)
        def on_close(sender, *args):
            # Covers the backdrop, the X and Escape, all of which bypass the
            # buttons and would otherwise leave the caller awaiting forever.
            self._finish(None)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------- ask

    async def ask(self, suggested_name):
        """
        Show the dialog and wait for the user.

        Returns {"name", "folder_id", "folder_name"} or None if cancelled.
        """
        self._name.value = suggested_name
        self._show_error("")
        self._future = asyncio.get_event_loop().create_future()
        self.modal.open()
        self._focus_name()
        return await self._future

    def _focus_name(self):
        try:
            self._name.dom_element.focus()
            self._name.dom_element.select()
        except Exception:
            # Focus is a convenience; never let it break the dialog.
            pass

    # --------------------------------------------------------------- internals

    def _on_key(self, dom_event):
        if getattr(dom_event, "key", None) == "Enter":
            dom_event.preventDefault()
            self._submit()

    def _set_folder(self, folder_id, folder_name):
        self._folder_id = folder_id
        self._folder_label.set_text(folder_name)

    def _show_error(self, message):
        self._error.set_text(message)
        self._error.style.display = "block" if message else "none"

    async def _choose_folder(self):
        try:
            picked = await self.session.pick_folder()
        except Exception as error:
            self._show_error(str(error))
            return
        if picked:
            self._set_folder(picked["id"], picked["name"])
            self._show_error("")

    def _submit(self):
        name = str(self._name.value or "").strip()
        if not name:
            self._show_error("Give the file a name.")
            return
        self._finish({
            "name": name,
            "folder_id": self._folder_id,
            "folder_name": self._folder_label.dom_element.textContent,
        })
        # Closing fires the modal's close event, which calls _finish(None);
        # that is harmless because the pending future has already been taken.
        self.modal.close()

    def _finish(self, result):
        """Resolve the waiter exactly once, whichever way the dialog ended."""
        future, self._future = self._future, None
        if future is not None and not future.done():
            future.set_result(result)
scripts/dashboard/save_tool_dialog.py:
"""
Saving the workflow, or one tool's steps, as a tool of the user's own, and
managing the tools saved that way.

The dialog says what the tool is called and which toolbox it lives in, which steps
to take (the whole workflow, or just a group a tool added), and which of their
options the tool should ask about each time it is run. The rest stay as they are
now. Making the tool is `tool_builder`'s job; this is the form.
"""
from antioch.dom import DOM
from antioch.elements import Button, Div, Input, Option, P, Select, Span
from antioch.event import when
from antioch.macros import Modal

from ui_lib import CheckboxGroup, labeled
from workflow_lib import ToolError

from . import nodes
from .node_dialog import _check_only
from .tool_builder import build_tool, candidates, option_label

NEW_TOOLBOX = "(a new toolbox…)"
WHOLE = "whole"
SELECTED = "selected"
BUTTON = {"background-color": "#34495e", "color": "#fff", "border": "none",
          "padding": "7px 16px", "cursor": "pointer", "font-size": "13px",
          "border-radius": "3px"}
SMALL = {"background-color": "#eef1f4", "color": "#333", "border": "1px solid #cfd6dd",
         "padding": "3px 9px", "cursor": "pointer", "font-size": "12px",
         "border-radius": "3px"}
MODAL_STYLE = {"max-width": "640px", "width": "92vw", "min-width": "0"}


class SaveToolDialog:
    """
    Usage:
        dialog = SaveToolDialog(panel)      # the WorkflowPanel
        dialog.open()
    """

    def __init__(self, panel):
        self._panel = panel
        self._selected = []         # the blocks selected when the dialog opened, in workflow order
        self._options = {}          # parameter label -> (step id, option)
        self._name = Input("text", placeholder="e.g. My provenance check",
                           style={"width": "280px"})
        self._toolbox = Select()
        self._new_toolbox = Input("text", placeholder="Toolbox name",
                                  style={"width": "200px", "margin-top": "6px"})
        self._description = Input("text", placeholder="What it is for (optional)",
                                  style={"width": "100%"})
        self._steps = Select()
        self._exposed = CheckboxGroup(all_checked=False, height="190px",
                                      empty_text="This selection has no options")
        self._status = Span("", style={"color": "#b00020", "font-size": "13px"})
        self._toolbox.on('change', lambda e: self._toolbox_changed())
        self._steps.on('change', lambda e: self._list_options())

        save = Button("Save tool", style=dict(BUTTON))

        @when(save.events.click)
        def on_save(sender, *args):
            self._save()

        form = Div(
            P("Turns steps you have wired up into a tool you can run again from the "
              "menus, with a short dialog of its own.",
              style={"color": "#555", "font-size": "13px", "margin": "0 0 14px 0"}),
            labeled("Name", self._name),
            labeled("Toolbox", Div(self._toolbox, self._new_toolbox),
                    "Tools are grouped into toolboxes, like the built-in ones"),
            labeled("Description", self._description),
            labeled("Steps to include", self._steps,
                    "The whole workflow, or just the steps one tool added"),
            labeled("Ask for these each time", self._exposed.element,
                    "Everything not ticked stays as it is now"),
            Div(save, self._status, style={"display": "flex", "gap": "12px",
                                            "align-items": "center"}),
            style={"padding": "16px 18px"})
        self.modal = Modal(title="Save as tool", modal_style=MODAL_STYLE)
        self.modal.set_content(form)
        DOM.add(self.modal.element)

    def open(self):
        panel = self._panel
        self._status.set_text("")
        self._name.value = ""
        self._description.value = ""
        self._fill_toolboxes()
        self._steps.clear()
        # What is selected on the canvas is what the tool is made from, if anything is.
        self._selected = panel.selected_steps()
        if self._selected:
            count = len(self._selected)
            self._steps.add(Option(f"The {count} selected block{'s' if count != 1 else ''}",
                                   value=SELECTED))
        self._steps.add(Option(f"The whole workflow ({len(panel.workflow.steps)} steps)",
                               value=WHOLE))
        for group, info in panel.workflow.groups.items():
            count = len(panel.workflow.members(group))
            self._steps.add(Option(f"{info['title'] or info['tool']} ({count} steps)",
                                   value=group))
        if self._selected:
            self._steps.value = SELECTED
        self._list_options()
        self.modal.open()

    def _fill_toolboxes(self):
        registry = self._panel.registry
        names = [n for n in registry.toolboxes()] or []
        if "My tools" not in names:
            names.append("My tools")
        self._toolbox.clear()
        for name in names:
            self._toolbox.add(Option(name, value=name))
        self._toolbox.add(Option(NEW_TOOLBOX, value=NEW_TOOLBOX))
        self._toolbox.value = "My tools"
        self._new_toolbox.value = ""
        self._toolbox_changed()

    def _toolbox_changed(self):
        self._new_toolbox.style.display = (
            "block" if self._toolbox.value == NEW_TOOLBOX else "none")

    def _chosen_steps(self):
        workflow = self._panel.workflow
        if self._steps.value == SELECTED:
            return [i for i in self._selected if any(s.id == i for s in workflow.steps)]
        if self._steps.value == WHOLE:
            return [s.id for s in workflow.steps]
        return workflow.members(self._steps.value)

    def _list_options(self):
        """Offer every option of the chosen steps; the data choices start ticked."""
        workflow = self._panel.workflow
        ids = self._chosen_steps()
        self._options, labels, ticked = {}, [], []
        for c in candidates(workflow, ids):
            label = option_label(workflow, c)       # numbered as the blocks are on the canvas
            self._options[label] = (c.step_id, c.option)
            labels.append(label)
            if c.exposed_by_default:
                ticked.append(label)
        self._exposed.set_options(labels)
        _check_only(self._exposed, ticked)

    def _save(self):
        panel = self._panel
        toolbox = (self._new_toolbox.value if self._toolbox.value == NEW_TOOLBOX
                   else self._toolbox.value)
        exposed = {self._options[label] for label in self._exposed.values()}
        try:
            tool = build_tool(
                panel.workflow, nodes.specs(), self._chosen_steps(),
                self._name.value, toolbox, self._description.value,
                exposed=exposed, taken=set(panel.registry.tools))
            panel.registry.add(tool)
        except ToolError as error:
            self._status.set_text(str(error))
            return
        self.modal.close()
        panel.say(f"Saved '{tool.label}' in the {tool.toolbox} toolbox. It is in the "
                  "menus now, and saved with the project.")


class ManageToolsDialog:
    """The tools the user has made, with a way to delete each."""

    def __init__(self, panel):
        self._panel = panel
        self._list = Div()
        self.modal = Modal(title="My tools", modal_style=MODAL_STYLE)
        self.modal.set_content(Div(self._list, style={"padding": "16px 18px"}))
        DOM.add(self.modal.element)

    def open(self):
        self._rebuild()
        self.modal.open()

    def _rebuild(self):
        registry = self._panel.registry
        self._list._dom_element.innerHTML = ""
        mine = [(k, t) for k, t in registry.tools.items() if not registry.is_builtin(k)]
        if not mine:
            self._list.add(P("No tools of your own yet. Wire up some steps and use "
                             "\"Save as tool…\".", style={"color": "#6c757d"}))
            return
        for key, tool in mine:
            remove = Button("Delete", style=dict(SMALL))

            @when(remove.events.click)
            def on_remove(sender, *args, key=key):
                registry.remove(key)
                self._rebuild()

            self._list.add(Div(
                Div(Span(tool.label, style={"font-weight": "600"}),
                    Span(f"  in {tool.toolbox}", style={"color": "#6c757d", "font-size": "12px"}),
                    P(tool.description or f"{len(tool.steps)} steps",
                      style={"margin": "2px 0 0 0", "font-size": "12px", "color": "#555"}),
                    style={"flex": "1"}),
                remove,
                style={"display": "flex", "align-items": "center", "gap": "10px",
                       "padding": "8px 0", "border-bottom": "1px solid #edf0f3"}))
scripts/dashboard/shell.py:
"""The page frame: header, top-level tabs, and the two panels.

Everything here is chrome. The tab bar is anchored and only the panel bodies scroll, so the
app behaves like an editor rather than a document.
"""
import asyncio

from antioch.dom import DOM
from antioch.elements import Button, Div, H1, Span
from antioch.event import when

from spreadsheet_lib import SpreadsheetUpload, TabulatorSheet
from ui_lib import TabItem, TabView

from .drive import DrivePanel
from .example_data import generate_example_rows
from .maps_panel import MapsPanel
from .project import ProjectPanel
from .prompt import PromptDialog
from .recovery import RecoveryStore
from .tracker import WorkTracker
from .workflow_panel import WorkflowPanel

# A definite height: Tabulator sizes its virtual viewport from this, and a
# percentage would resolve against an auto-height parent and collapse.
TABLE_HEIGHT = "calc(100vh - 262px)"

PANEL_STYLE = {
    "display": "flex", "flex-direction": "column",
    "height": "100%", "min-height": "0",
}
SCROLL_STYLE = {
    "flex": "1", "min-height": "0", "overflow-y": "auto", "padding": "16px",
}

ROW_BUTTON_STYLE = {
    "background-color": "#34495e", "color": "#fff", "border": "none",
    "padding": "6px 14px", "cursor": "pointer", "font-size": "13px",
    "margin-right": "8px",
}
STATUS_STYLE = {"font-size": "13px", "color": "#6c757d"}


class AppShell:
    """
    Builds and mounts the page.

    Attributes:
        table    - TabulatorSheet holding the data
        upload   - SpreadsheetUpload above it
        drive    - DrivePanel beside it; empty and hidden when Google
                   sign-in is not configured
        project  - ProjectPanel: the title-bar Projects button and its dialog
        tracker  - WorkTracker: unsaved-work marker, recovery copy, autosave
        recovery - RecoveryStore: the IndexedDB recovery copy
        workflow_panel - the Workflow tab: the canvas, its tools and blocks, and each block's
                   output
        maps     - MapsPanel: the Maps tab — delineate watersheds and fetch gauges and climate,
                   handing the results to the workflow
        tabs     - top-level TabView (Workflow, Spreadsheet, then Maps)
    """

    def __init__(self, title="Sed/Stats"):
        self._style_body()

        self.table = TabulatorSheet(data=generate_example_rows(), height=TABLE_HEIGHT)
        self.upload = SpreadsheetUpload()
        self.drive = DrivePanel(get_rows=self.table.get_data)
        # The workflow panel does not exist yet, so its state is fetched lazily.
        self.project = ProjectPanel(
            self.drive, get_rows=self.table.get_data,
            get_workflow=lambda: self.workflow_panel.to_dict())

        @when(self.drive.events.sign_in_change)
        def on_sign_in_change(sender, usable, *args):
            self.project.set_enabled(usable)
            # Whether leaving the page loses work depends on being able to save.
            self.tracker.changed()
        DOM.add(self._header(title))

        # Watches the sheet and the workflow for unsaved work: marks the
        # Projects button, warns before leaving, keeps a recovery copy in
        # IndexedDB and, if opted in, autosaves the open project.
        self.recovery = RecoveryStore()
        self.tracker = WorkTracker(
            self.table.get_data, lambda: self.workflow_panel.to_dict(), self.project,
            self.recovery, self.table,
            drive_usable=lambda: (self.drive.session.signed_in
                                  and self.drive.session.has_drive_access))
        self.project.guard = self.tracker.confirm_discard
        # The workflow's steps are part of the work, so editing them counts.
        # A step's output lives with its block, so there is nowhere else to look for results.
        # "Save to Drive" is offered only when there is a Drive to save to.
        self.workflow_panel = WorkflowPanel(
            self.table.get_data, on_change=self.tracker.changed,
            on_save=self.drive.save_bytes if self.drive.configured else None,
            set_rows=self.table.set_data,
            on_view_spreadsheet=lambda: self.tabs.set_active(1),
            on_view_map=self._view_on_map)
        self.maps = MapsPanel(self.table.get_data, self.workflow_panel)

        self.tabs = TabView(fill=True, tabs=[
            TabItem("Workflow", self._workflow_tab()),
            TabItem("Spreadsheet", self._spreadsheet_panel()),
            TabItem("Maps", Div(self.maps.element, style=dict(PANEL_STYLE))),
        ])
        DOM.add(Div(self.tabs.element, style={
            "flex": "1", "min-height": "0", "padding": "0 16px 16px",
            "display": "flex", "flex-direction": "column",
        }))

    def _view_on_map(self, step_id):
        """A Watershed block's "View on the map": open the Maps tab and show it."""
        self.tabs.set_active(2)
        self.maps.show_block(step_id)

    @staticmethod
    def _style_body():
        # Viewport-height flex column with no page scroll, so the tab bar and
        # toolbar stay put and only the panels scroll.
        DOM.body.style.update({
            "margin": "0",
            "height": "100vh",
            "overflow": "hidden",
            "display": "flex",
            "flex-direction": "column",
            "font-family": "system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif",
        })

    def _header(self, title):
        return Div(
            H1(title, style={"margin": "0", "font-size": "20px"}),
            # Right-aligned together. The Projects button comes first, so it
            # sits to the left of the signed-in email; both are hidden when
            # Google sign-in is not configured or the user is signed out.
            Div(self.project.button_element, self.drive.account_element, style={
                "margin-left": "auto", "display": "flex",
                "align-items": "center", "gap": "12px",
            }),
            style={
                "flex-shrink": "0", "padding": "10px 16px",
                "background-color": "#2c3e50", "color": "#fff",
                "display": "flex", "align-items": "center", "gap": "12px",
            },
        )

    def _row_controls(self):
        """
        Row and column buttons, and undo.

        Tabulator has no built-in affordance for these, and a spreadsheet the user is
        expected to edit needs them. Deleting works on whatever the current selection
        touches — click a row number or a column header, or drag a range. The same things,
        and renaming a column, are on the right-click menus of the rows and the headers.
        """
        add = Button("Add row", style=ROW_BUTTON_STYLE)
        add_column = Button("Add column", style=ROW_BUTTON_STYLE)
        delete = Button("Delete selected rows", style=ROW_BUTTON_STYLE)
        delete_columns = Button("Delete selected columns", style=ROW_BUTTON_STYLE)
        undo = Button("Undo", style=ROW_BUTTON_STYLE)
        redo = Button("Redo", style=ROW_BUTTON_STYLE)
        status = Span("", style=STATUS_STYLE)
        self.table.on_message = status.set_text
        self.table.prompt = PromptDialog().ask

        @when(add.events.click)
        def on_add(sender, *args):
            self.table.add_row()
            status.set_text("Row added.")

        @when(add_column.events.click)
        def on_add_column(sender, *args):
            asyncio.ensure_future(self.table.request_add_column())

        @when(delete.events.click)
        def on_delete(sender, *args):
            removed = self.table.delete_selected_rows()
            status.set_text(
                f"Deleted {removed} row{'s' if removed != 1 else ''}."
                if removed else
                "Nothing selected — click a row number, or drag across cells.")

        @when(delete_columns.events.click)
        def on_delete_columns(sender, *args):
            removed = self.table.delete_selected_columns()
            status.set_text(
                f"Deleted {removed} column{'s' if removed != 1 else ''}."
                if removed else
                "Nothing selected — click a column header, or drag across cells.")

        @when(undo.events.click)
        def on_undo(sender, *args):
            status.set_text("Undone." if self.table.undo() else "Nothing to undo.")

        @when(redo.events.click)
        def on_redo(sender, *args):
            status.set_text("Redone." if self.table.redo() else "Nothing to redo.")

        return Div(add, add_column, delete, delete_columns, undo, redo, status, style={
            "display": "flex", "align-items": "center", "flex-wrap": "wrap",
            "gap": "4px",
        })

    def _spreadsheet_panel(self):
        return Div(
            Div(self.upload.element, self.drive.element, style={
                "flex-shrink": "0", "padding": "10px 16px",
                "border-bottom": "1px solid #e9ecef",
                "display": "flex", "align-items": "center",
                "flex-wrap": "wrap", "gap": "8px",
            }),
            Div(self._row_controls(), style={
                "flex-shrink": "0", "padding": "10px 16px",
                "border-bottom": "1px solid #e9ecef",
            }),
            Div(self.table.element, style={
                "flex": "1", "min-height": "0", "padding": "16px",
            }),
            style=PANEL_STYLE,
        )

    def _workflow_tab(self):
        return Div(Div(self.workflow_panel.element, style=SCROLL_STYLE),
                   style=PANEL_STYLE)
scripts/dashboard/step_menu.py:
"""
What a right-click on the canvas offers.

Kept apart from the widgets so what each menu says, and when an item is greyed, can be tested
without a browser. An item is (key, label, enabled); None is a divider.
"""


def node_menu(has_output, has_charts, can_save, multiple_charts=False, can_write=False,
              can_view_map=False, has_message=False):
    """
    The menu of a step.

    Args:
        has_output: the step has run and made something to show
        has_charts: that output includes plots, so there is something to download
        can_save: a Google Drive is connected to save to
        multiple_charts: the download is a zip of plots, not one SVG
        can_write: the step has run and made a table, which can replace the spreadsheet
        can_view_map: the step holds a watershed, which the Maps tab can show
        has_message: the step failed or was skipped, and says why
    """
    items = [
        ("edit", "Edit…", True),
        ("run", "Run this step", True),
        None,
        ("output", "Show output", has_output),
        ("download", "Download as zip of SVGs" if multiple_charts else "Download SVG",
         has_output and has_charts),
    ]
    if has_message:
        items.insert(4, ("message", "Show the whole message", True))
    if can_save:
        items.append(("save", "Save to Drive", has_output and has_charts))
    if can_view_map:
        items += [None, ("view_map", "View on the map", True)]
    if can_write:
        items += [None, ("to_sheet", "Replace the spreadsheet with this table…", True)]
    items += [None, ("duplicate", "Duplicate", True), ("delete", "Delete", True)]
    return items


def selection_menu(count):
    """What a right-click offers on several selected blocks at once."""
    return [("run_selected", f"Run {count} blocks", True),
            ("save_tool", f"Save {count} blocks as a tool…", True),
            None,
            ("delete_selected", f"Delete {count} blocks…", True)]


def data_menu():
    """The spreadsheet block has one thing to offer: going to the spreadsheet."""
    return [("view_sheet", "View Spreadsheet", True)]


def edge_menu():
    return [("disconnect", "Disconnect", True)]


def canvas_menu(has_steps):
    return [
        ("run_all", "Run workflow", has_steps),
        ("tidy", "Tidy up the layout", has_steps),
        ("zoom_reset", "Zoom to 100%", True),
        None,
        ("clear", "Remove every step…", has_steps),
    ]
scripts/dashboard/tables.py:
"""
Result tables, as read-only Tabulator sheets.

Outputs are read, selected through and copied out of — a comparison matrix goes
into a paper, a contribution table into a caption — so they get a real grid
rather than a static <table>: range selection and clipboard copy.

Every column is data, including the first. Sample names are a measured column
like any other and are selected, copied and aligned on the same terms, rather
than being treated as a row header the grid draws differently.

Editing is off throughout. These cells are computed; typing into one would
change nothing and imply otherwise.
"""
import js

from antioch.elements import Div
from spreadsheet_lib import TabulatorSheet

# Fields are generated rather than taken from the titles. A Tabulator field
# containing a dot is a nested-property accessor, and sample names are free to
# contain anything at all.
FIELD_PREFIX = "c"

ROW_HEIGHT = 30
HEADER_HEIGHT = 40
# Past this many rows the sheet scrolls rather than growing; a per-sample
# table stays short, but nothing stops someone loading forty samples.
MAX_VISIBLE_ROWS = 14


# Cells that stand in for a value rather than being one. A column of these
# plus numbers is still a numeric column.
PLACEHOLDERS = {"", "—", "-", "n/a", "na", "nan"}


def _is_numeric(value) -> bool:
    text = str(value).strip()
    if text.lower() in PLACEHOLDERS:
        return True
    try:
        float(text.replace(",", ""))
    except ValueError:
        return False
    return True


def _alignment(values) -> str:
    """
    Right-align a column of numbers, left-align anything else.

    Decided from what a column holds rather than where it sits, so the first
    column is aligned by the same rule as the rest. A column of all
    placeholders has nothing to align on and reads fine either way.
    """
    if any(str(v).strip().lower() not in PLACEHOLDERS for v in values) and \
            all(_is_numeric(v) for v in values):
        return "right"
    return "left"


# What the tables built since the last `begin_previews` held, so a block that shows a table (a matrix,
# a per-sample summary) can have a thumbnail of it without each block saying so. Kept as titles and a
# few rows, which is all a thumbnail draws.
_PREVIEWS = []
PREVIEW_ROWS = 8


def begin_previews():
    """Start noting the tables that are built."""
    _PREVIEWS.clear()


def first_preview():
    """(titles, rows) of the first table built since `begin_previews`, or None."""
    return _PREVIEWS[0] if _PREVIEWS else None


def result_table(titles, rows, sortable=False):
    """
    A read-only sheet.

    Args:
        titles: column headings
        rows: one list of cell values per row, matching `titles` in length
        sortable: header sorting. Off by default — a comparison matrix's rows
            and columns have to stay in the same order to read as a matrix,
            and every table here shares the plot's sample order.

    Returns:
        A Div wrapping the sheet, with `.sheet` on it for the caller.
    """
    if len(_PREVIEWS) < 20:
        _PREVIEWS.append(([str(t) for t in titles], [list(r) for r in rows[:PREVIEW_ROWS]]))
    fields = [f"{FIELD_PREFIX}{index}" for index in range(len(titles))]
    columns = []
    for index, (field, title) in enumerate(zip(fields, titles)):
        column_values = [row[index] if index < len(row) else "" for row in rows]
        columns.append({
            "title": str(title),
            "field": field,
            "headerSort": sortable,
            "headerHozAlign": "center",
            "hozAlign": _alignment(column_values),
            "minWidth": 90,
        })

    data = [dict(zip(fields, ["" if v is None else v for v in row]))
            for row in rows]

    visible = min(len(data), MAX_VISIBLE_ROWS)
    height = (HEADER_HEIGHT + visible * ROW_HEIGHT + 2
              if len(data) > MAX_VISIBLE_ROWS else None)

    sheet = TabulatorSheet(
        data=data,
        columns=columns,
        height=f"{height}px" if height else None,
        options={
            "layout": "fitDataFill",
            # Sample names may contain dots; without this Tabulator would read
            # them as nested-property paths and find nothing.
            "nestedFieldSeparator": False,
            "movableColumns": False,
            # A row-number gutter, as a spreadsheet has. It is not decoration:
            # with row selection on, Tabulator's range module claims the first
            # visible column as its row header — skipping it in every range
            # (`start.col = 1`) and dropping it from the copy. Giving it a
            # column of its own is what keeps the first *data* column being
            # data, selectable and copied like the rest.
            "rowHeader": {
                "formatter": "rownum",
                "hozAlign": "center",
                "headerSort": False,
                "resizable": False,
                "frozen": True,
                "width": 44,
            },
            # The point of a grid over a static table: select a block of
            # results and paste it somewhere useful.
            "selectableRange": True,
            "selectableRangeColumns": True,
            "selectableRangeRows": True,
            "clipboard": "copy",
            "clipboardCopyRowRange": "range",
            # Column headings travel with the copy; the row-number gutter does
            # not, since it is numbering rather than data.
            "clipboardCopyConfig": {"columnHeaders": True, "rowHeaders": False},
            "placeholder": "Nothing to show",
        },
    )

    _ensure_css()
    wrapper = Div(sheet.element, style={"max-width": "100%"})
    wrapper.sheet = sheet
    _redraw_when_shown(sheet, wrapper)
    return wrapper


def _redraw_when_shown(sheet, wrapper):
    """
    Redraw the sheet the first time it has a size.

    Tabulator measures itself on render. A table built inside a hidden tab —
    every tab but the first, in a multi-dimension output — measures zero and
    draws as an empty strip. Watching for the element gaining width fixes it
    wherever it is mounted, without the gallery or the tab view needing to
    know a table is in there.
    """
    element = wrapper._dom_element

    def on_resize(entries, observer):
        # Nothing here may raise: this runs from a browser callback, where an
        # exception surfaces as an uncaught error rather than anything useful.
        try:
            if element.offsetWidth > 0:
                sheet.redraw()
        except Exception:
            pass

    try:
        observer = js.ResizeObserver.new(sheet._create_proxy(on_resize))
        observer.observe(element)
        # Held on the macro so the proxy and observer outlive this call.
        sheet._result_observer = observer
    except Exception:
        # Without ResizeObserver the table still renders; it just may need a
        # tab switch to size itself.
        pass


_CSS_ID = "dashboard-result-table-css"
_CSS = """
.tabulator .tabulator-header { border-bottom: 2px solid #b8b2a8; }
.tabulator .tabulator-col { background-color: #f6f3ee; }
"""


def _ensure_css():
    # Not `is None`: Pyodide represents JS null as a `jsnull` sentinel, so
    # `is None` never matched and this re-injected the style on every call.
    if not js.document.getElementById(_CSS_ID):
        style = js.document.createElement("style")
        style.id = _CSS_ID
        style.textContent = _CSS
        js.document.head.appendChild(style)
